pr_body:
Fixes #29932

## Description

Adds `TimeSpan` support to System.Text.Json JsonSerializer.

Uses [Utf8Parser.TryParse](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.buffers.text.utf8parser.tryparse?view=net-5.0#System_Buffers_Text_Utf8Parser_TryParse_System_ReadOnlySpan_System_Byte__System_TimeSpan__System_Int32__System_Char_) & [Utf8Formatter.TryFormat](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.buffers.text.utf8formatter.tryformat?view=net-5.0#System_Buffers_Text_Utf8Formatter_TryFormat_System_TimeSpan_System_Span_System_Byte__System_Int32__System_Buffers_StandardFormat_) for the heavy lifting.

## Public API Changes

```csharp
    public static partial class JsonMetadataServices
    {
       public static System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonConverter<System.TimeSpan> TimeSpanConverter { get { throw null; } }
    }
```

## Considerations

This is using the constant ("c") format. I think the general short format ("g") could compact things a bit, but not sure if that would round-trip with Newtonsoft and it is culture-sensitive.

/cc @layomia @eiriktsarpalis @JamesNK

issue_context.title: JsonSerializer support for TimeSpan in 3.0?

review_comments:
nit
```suggestion
            static void Test(string testString, bool isFinalBlock)
```
Echoing https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/54186/files#r651698255, might make sense to include `TimeSpan.MaxValue`/`MinValue` as inputs here.
Updated

Following Json.NET's example, the deserializer should probably also recognize `G/g` formatted timespans as well, e.g. `"9999999:23:59:59"`.

I would also include boundary values here, such as the serializations for `TimeSpan.MaxValue/MinValue`.
It might be worth investigating if Json.NET supports other formats too.

* I added some logic in `TimeSpanConverter` so that it will try 'g' format if 'c' is unsuccessful. People using 'c' will get optimal perf, people using 'g' will take a hit. Other option is to copy the `Utf8Parser.TryParse` code and tweak it for our needs. Those tweaks could lower the perf of 'c' case since it will need to also encompass the 'g' logic. Let me know what you think about this!

* It looks like Json.NET calls into `TimeSpan.ToString()` & `TimeSpan.Parse`:

   * https://github.com/JamesNK/Newtonsoft.Json/blob/f7e7bd05d9280f17993500085202ff4ea150564a/Src/Newtonsoft.Json/JsonTextWriter.cs#L751
 
   * https://github.com/JamesNK/Newtonsoft.Json/blob/f7e7bd05d9280f17993500085202ff4ea150564a/Src/Newtonsoft.Json/Utilities/ConvertUtils.cs#L253

   `TimeSpan.ToString()` uses the 'c' format so our write is compatible. `TimeSpan.Parse` is a little more fuzzy about what it accepts [which can lead to some surprises](https://blog.macrosssoftware.com/index.php/2020/06/04/timespan-parse240000-may-surprise-you/). I updated the tests to show that we round-trip with Json.NET for the most part, but break on that one known case. Let me know what you think about that!
I'd be interested to see the performance impact of `TimeSpan.Parse` versus the `Utf8Parser` fallback approach first for both 'c' and 'g' formats.
Thanks, I think we can use Utf8Parser for now but could reconsider in the future if other use cases crop up. cc @layomia @steveharter for second opinions.

Since there is a perf implication here, I think it's better to support just the 'c' format for now since it is the default output of `Newtonsoft.Json` and should cover most scenarios. We can adjust based on user feedback. This is in keeping with support for other primitives where we use just one format. It is easy to write a custom converter for other formats.
Removed the 'g' fallback
This isn't being  used (it should).
Updated

If you're relying on `Utf8Parser.TryParse(..., out TimeSpan, ...)`, please also add these unit tests:

```cs
[InlineData("\\t23:59:59")] // should succeed since Utf8Parser.TryParse drops leading horizontal tab chars
[InlineData("\t23:59:59")] // should fail since illegal JSON string
```
Added. They both fail now due to some logic added checking for leading whitespace.

Due to other logic, we should be fine, but a few more nullable `TimeSpan` tests would be good. E.g. deserializing `null` into a non-nullable `TimeSpan` should fail, but should be fine for nullable `TimeSpan?`.
Why delete this helper?

It wasn't being used anymore so I cleaned it up. The code that was calling it (in Utf8JsonReader.TryGet) is now calling `IsInRangeInclusive` directly so it can pass in the max length based on encoded string or not. You want me to put it back with the other feedback items for a follow-up?
I don't think we have `DateTimeOffset` failure tests for leading whitespace. We'd take a follow up to add these.
I was going to add a comment about there needing to be tests exercising the new API, but I couldn't find a test class doing this for the existing `JsonMetadataServices` converters. cc @layomia

Since this is being [initialized](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0248a1529654fe99bb029b2a77728a0dbf5f0c6a/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonSerializerOptions.Converters.cs#L75) on start-up, the new tests in this PR exercise this property. When we add corresponding source-gen support for `TimeSpan`, we'll also add tests for that scenario.

[Non-blocking for this PR] When https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/54254 goes in, we should consider updating this to use the new `Utf8JsonWriter.WriteRawValue` API so we can avoid logic that checks whether the input payload needs to be escaped. We'd first need to quote the formatted value.

Thanks for these changes. Searching for "stackalloc byte" in the STJ.csproj shows there might be a few more places that would benefit from this pattern, particularly in `JsonReaderHelper.*.cs`. We'd take a follow up PR to address this if you're up for it!
Please include boundary values such as the serializations of `TimeSpan.MaxValue + 1 tick` and `TimeSpan.MinValue - 1 tick`.
Also, testing against non-string JSON values might be useful here.

* Added the `TimeSpan.MaxValue` \ `TimeSpan.MinValue` cases.

* Added some non-string JSON value cases.
